paragraphs.text: Local knowledge base for DSH: BM25 + hybrid retrieval with cited passages (Markdown/TXT/PDF, offline
). Indexes the memory files written by dsh-memory-archiver.
# dsh-kb-lite
Local knowledge base for DeepSeek Harness: ingest Markdown, text and PDF files, retrieve passages wi
th BM25 or optional dense search, and hand the model citations it can point at — file, heading, line
r optional dense search, and hand the model citations it can point at — file, heading, line or page.
English | 简体中文
> **0.4.11** — `kb_search` / `kb_ask` now down-weight documents whose front matter says `status: sup
erseded` (×0.3); pass `include_superseded: true` to rank them normally. Earlier, 0.4.10 added the `o
rphaned` / `superseded` counts, and 0.4.4 added `kb_sync` and index-freshness reporting.
MIT. Host-only DSH plugin, six tools, no browser UI, and the engine opens no sockets. BM25 needs not
hing beyond the Python standard library.
## Why another one
`dsh-kb-rag` is the closest existing plugin, and it cannot be installed on DSH 0.2.0-rc.2. It declar
es a `dsh.client.inject` entry for `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime`, and that package is not part o
f the 0.2.0-rc.2 client baseline. It also pins `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` to `^0.1.0-rc.6`, which is t
he range DSH's own version gate rejects when the host is 0.2.0-rc.2. Every published version — 22 of
them at the time of writing — carries the same peer range, so there is no older release to fall bac
at the time of writing — carries the same peer range, so there is no older release to fall back to.
This plugin takes the other side of that trade: host-only, no client bundle, no client injection, an
d peer ranges written with an explicit prerelease branch so `0.2.0-rc.x` actually matches. Nothing i
s wrong with the idea of `dsh-kb-rag` — the blocker is the client dependency and the peer range, not
the feature set. If a release appears that targets 0.2.x without injecting `dsh-client-runtime`, it
will cover much of the same ground and there is no reason to prefer this one.
The scope is deliberately smaller than a full RAG stack: six tools, one local index directory, and a
BM25 path that works on a machine where you have never installed torch.
## Features

- Six tools: `kb_ingest`, `kb_search`, `kb_ask`, `kb_stats`, `kb_sync`, `kb_clear`.
- No browser UI
and no client bundle. `package.json` deliberately has no `dsh.client` field: the plugin only adds ho
st tools, so a DSH release that changes client APIs cannot break an installed copy. That matters bec

ause a broken client half takes the whole web UI down with it — DSH starts all-or-nothing.
- Input:
`.md`, `.markdown`, `.txt`, `.pdf`. PDF needs `pymupdf`; without it each PDF shows up as a per-file
error and the rest of the batch still indexes. Other extensions are not read: a directory walk skips

them, and a file you name explicitly is reported as `unsupported_extension`.
- Recursive directory
ingest — hidden directories and `.git`, `node_modules`, `.venv`, `__pycache__` and similar are skipp
ed. Incremental by `sha256`: unchanged files are skipped, changed files are re-indexed, `force: true
` re-parses regardless. `prune: true` drops documents whose files no longer exist under the paths yo

u pass.
- `max_files` caps one call; anything over the cap is returned as `pending` so the next call

can pick it up.
- BM25 with no third-party dependency, including CJK bigram tokenisation.
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

- **Node.js 18 or newer** — the host side of the plugin.
- **Python 3.9 or newer** — for the engine.

- **Nothing else** for BM25.
- Optional, for PDF: `pymupdf` (`pip install pymupdf`).
- Optional, fo
r dense retrieval: `numpy` and `sentence-transformers` (`pip install numpy sentence-transformers`),

in the interpreter the plugin launches (see `KB_LITE_PYTHON`).
- No database, no service, no API key

n the interpreter the plugin launches (see `KB_LITE_PYTHON`).
- No database, no service, no API key.
## Limitations
These are known and not hidden behind configuration:

- **No reranker.** Hybrid fuses BM25 and dense ranks; nothing re-scores the fused list afterwards.
-
**No DOI or citation-link handling.** A DOI in a PDF is text like any other. `kb_ask` gives you pat

h, line and page, not a clickable reference.
- **No Zotero (or any bibliography) import.** Point `kb

_ingest` at files on disk; that is the only entry point.
- **No OCR.** A scanned PDF has no text lay

er, so it yields nothing. Run OCR yourself first and ingest the text.
- **No incremental vector-stor
e update.** Every ingest rewrites the whole vector file to match the new chunk list; unchanged chunk

s reuse their cached embeddings, but there is no append and no background compaction.
- **The BM25 i
ndex is rebuilt per query, not cached.** That is fine for the intended size (hundreds of files, thou
sands of chunks) and it keeps the on-disk format trivial; it is not the design to pick for a hundred
-thousand-chunk corpus. Measured on this machine: 25 chunks answer a query in milliseconds; the cost

grows with the corpus, not with the query.
- **Chunk size is fixed per ingest batch.** `chunk_chars
` and `chunk_overlap` are per-call; there is no per-file override, and the whole corpus shares one s

etting.
- **Four extensions only.** `.md`, `.markdown`, `.txt`, `.pdf`. DOCX, HTML and EPUB are not

read.
- **The engine is a per-plugin-instance process, not a shared daemon.** Each DSH instance that
loads the plugin starts its own `python engine/kb_engine.py`. Two profiles mean two processes, each
loading its own copy of the embedding model if dense retrieval is on — not one shared service.
## Privacy
- The engine opens **no sockets** and makes no network requests. There is no telemetry, no update ch

eck, no remote index.
- The only long-lived process it spawns is one local `python engine/kb_engine.
py` per plugin instance. Before that it runs a one-shot interpreter check, described in `SECURITY.md

`.
- What it reads: the files you pass to `kb_ingest`, and its own `kb_root`.
- What it writes: only

inside `kb_root`.
- No credentials are read or stored. There is no key, token or account.
One caveat, because it is easy to get wrong: if you install the optional dense stack, `sentence-tran
sformers` (not this plugin) downloads `BAAI/bge-small-zh-v1.5` from Hugging Face the first time it r
uns, unless the model is already in your local cache. Pre-populate the cache, or skip the dense extr
as, on a machine that must not egress.
`SECURITY.md` has the exact argv, the full read/write boundary, and commands you can run to check al
l of the above yourself.
